capabilities.target: Chat reply to the authenticated requester

inputs.source: Engineering design docs retrieved via docs.search
Jira tickets filed by customers (planned MCP connection)

instructions.note: The instruction tells the agent to answer using docs.search without scoping retrieval to the asker's role or clearance, so any authenticated employee's question reaches the full confidential corpus.
The only safeguard against leaking secrets or over-broad disclosure is a prompt rule, not a technical access control or output filter.

controls.name: Prompt restricts tool use to docs.search with a citation requirement
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to follow the instruction; a more capable or adversarially prompted model can reason past it.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never paste secrets or credentials into answers
controls.decay_rationale: The model must choose to comply; a more capable model follows longer, more convincing injected goals and can rationalize exceptions.

controls.name: docs.search credential is read-only
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the credential grant itself; model behavior cannot expand it to write or delete. Does not scope which documents can be read.

controls.name: Chat replies are delivered only to the authenticated requester
controls.decay_rationale: The destination comes from the authenticated session, not from model output, so it does not decay with capability. It stops the agent from being redirected to send output elsewhere, but it does not verify that the requester is entitled to the retrieved content.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Blocks covert exfiltration via markdown image or link rendering client-side; unaffected by model capability. Does not cover a future tool that itself makes outbound requests.

controls.name: No network egress today
controls.decay_rationale: No capability in the current design can make outbound network requests, so data cannot leave the organization's network today. This control is removed by design the moment the planned web.fetch tool is added.

controls.name: Per-document authorization check against the requester's role
Destination allowlist and URL-construction restriction for web.fetch
Untrusted-content tagging and isolation for Jira ticket content

findings.title: Confused deputy (TC4): docs.search credential is broader than any individual requester's own entitlement

attack_path.note: Any SSO-authenticated employee can ask, regardless of whether they are an engineer.
The agent's read-only credential can access the full confidential corpus, not scoped to the asker's entitlement.
Confidential content is disclosed to the asking employee even if they would not otherwise be authorized to read the source document.

forecast.watch_signal: New document sources added to docs.search, or a policy change expanding who may query confidential engineering content, without an accompanying entitlement check.

evidence.observation: States only engineers can write to design docs but does not restrict who may read them via the agent; any SSO-authenticated employee can ask questions.
Instruction 'Answer engineering questions using docs.search' does not scope retrieval to the asker's role or clearance.

recommendations.action: Filter docs.search results to only documents the authenticated requester is entitled to read, enforced at retrieval time, before content enters the model context.
Log which documents were retrieved and surfaced per request, tied to requester identity, to support entitlement audits.

findings.title: Indirect prompt injection via engineering design docs (ASI01) targeting instruction override

attack_path.note: Engineering design doc content enters the model context un-sanitized through search results.
The read tool surfaces the document, including any instructions embedded in it by its author.
Only a prompt rule, not a structural control, stops the agent from pasting secrets if an embedded instruction tries to override its goal.

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version string changes in config, or the agent begins handling longer multi-turn sessions, either of which weakens the behavioral instructions this finding relies on.

evidence.observation: The only control against leaking sensitive content is the instruction 'Never paste secrets or credentials into answers,' which is behavioral and depends on model compliance.
Design docs are authored internally and enter the model's context through docs.search with no stated sanitization or instruction-detection step.

recommendations.action: Add an input-side classifier or provenance tag on retrieved document content that flags imperative instructions aimed at the agent, and quarantine flagged content before it reaches the model.
Move the secret and credential filter out of the prompt and into a structural output scanner that blocks known credential patterns before a reply is sent, independent of model compliance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): planned web.fetch plus Jira MCP server removes the only current egress control

attack_path.note: A customer-filed ticket contains hidden instructions targeting the agent (indirect injection from an untrusted external author).
The agent searches confidential engineering design docs in the course of answering the original question.
The planned tool fetches an attacker-chosen URL, embedding retrieved confidential content in the request and exfiltrating it outside the org.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest diff adds web.fetch; MCP client config diff adds a Jira server entry; either roadmap item ships without an accompanying egress allowlist or untrusted-content handling.

evidence.observation: Roadmap: add a web.fetch tool so answers can include public references, and connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers — a new egress channel plus a new untrusted input source, introduced together.
'There is no network egress today' is the only control this roadmap item removes; no replacement control is mentioned alongside it.

recommendations.action: Before enabling web.fetch, restrict it to an allowlist of destinations and block the model from constructing request URLs that embed content retrieved from docs.search.
Tag Jira ticket content as untrusted at ingestion and keep it out of any session that also has confidential-doc read access and network egress, or add an injection filter at the MCP boundary.
Add egress monitoring and alerting on web.fetch calls with unusually long query strings or encoded payloads.

governance_refs.note: Both roadmap items are significant changes requiring reassessment before launch.

rating.rationale: Present-day risk is driven by two architecture gaps: docs.search grants every authenticated employee read access to the full confidential engineering corpus with no per-requester entitlement check (F1, residual high, no control credits), and the only defense against embedded-instruction injection from those same docs is a prompt rule (F2, residual moderate after behavioral-control credit). Neither of these is addressed by the roadmap. The forecast jumps to critical because the two planned additions arrive together: web.fetch creates the first outbound network egress channel, and the Jira MCP connection creates the first genuinely untrusted (customer-authored) input, completing a lethal trifecta (F3) the moment both ship, with the current no-egress control the one thing standing between today's design and that outcome. No approval gate currently exists on any capability.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior; no logs, traces, or live testing were reviewed.

No MCP config or tool manifest was provided for docs.search, so whether it already enforces per-user document scoping is inferred rather than verified; confidence on Finding 1 is set to medium accordingly.
The web.fetch tool and Jira MCP server are roadmap items, not yet built; Finding 3 is a forecast based on the stated plan and assumes no additional controls ship with them, since none were described.
Attack paths were limited to 6 steps per the toxic-combination search procedure; all paths identified here are within that limit.
